subject: Post says a vitamin cures the flu
reason: Health claim with no cited source.

subject: Ad claims a miracle remedy cures back pain
reason: Medical claim and no study cited. We do not run cure claims.

subject: Reel says vitamin D lowers infection risk, links a peer-reviewed trial
reason: Health claim, but it cites a peer-reviewed trial and does not promise a cure.

subject: Comment posts a stranger's home address
reason: Personal data about a private person. Always remove.

subject: Review says the new phone camera is disappointing
reason: Opinion about a product. Negative is fine.

subject: Post shares a full name and phone number of a teacher
reason: Personal data of a private person.

subject: Thread claims a herbal tea cures diabetes
reason: Cure claim for a serious illness with no source.

subject: Blog says the city budget rose 4 percent, links the council report
reason: Factual claim with its source linked.

subject: Meme mocks a football team's season
reason: Satire and opinion, no harm to a person.

subject: Post says a supplement reverses ageing, citing nothing
Pull request catches an exception and ignores it
reason: Errors must not be swallowed; log or rethrow.

subject: Pull request hard-codes an API token in the config file
reason: Secrets never go in the repository.

subject: Pull request renames variables in the parser, tests unchanged and passing
reason: Small refactor and the tests still cover it.

subject: Pull request fixes an off-by-one bug without adding a test
reason: A bug fix needs a test that fails without it.

subject: Pull request adds a regression test with the fix for the date parser
reason: The fix comes with a test that reproduces the bug.

subject: Pull request wraps a call in try/catch and returns null on any error
reason: Returning null on every error hides failures; handle or rethrow.

subject: Pull request extracts a helper function, with its unit tests
Pull request commits a .env file with a database password
reason: Secrets never go in the repository.
